data.summary: BunnyEvents is four repos under one folder: backend (Supabase: migrations, row-level security and edge functions, the contract), app (the Flutter iOS app: attendee, host and door), console (TanStack Start on Vercel: host manage, admin and public pages) and board (the decision record), with the connectors SDK outside the trust boundary. The backend owns the schema; the app and the console each generate their own types from it and no code crosses a repo, so a cross-surface change lands backend-first as an additive migration. Reads and per-user writes go from both clients straight to Supabase under row-level security; every privileged verb is a named Edge Function running as the service role, and a function starts closed until a migration grants it to its real caller. Events enter the catalog only through ingest-events; pg_cron pumps the notification outbox every five minutes and pulls the event sources daily. Ticket payments are simulated today and Stripe is in test mode. Hosted runs on one interim Supabase project while the main one is inactive; the console's production is app.bunny.events.

crossing.rule: Reads and per-user writes go straight from both clients to Supabase under row-level security; every table's policies are proved against a two- and three-user matrix before ship.

Every privileged verb is a named Edge Function running as the service role, and a function starts closed: the migration that adds it grants execute to its real caller (check-fn-grants is the backstop).
An admin act passes is_app_admin and writes a moderation_actions row; the console's admin pages are a thin client of admin-actions.
ingest-events is the one external write door into the catalog: service role only, provenance on every row, and a new connector's first rows stay staged until approved.
Money: ticket payments are simulated and Stripe stays in test mode; checkout refuses until the payment seam is switched to real.
The schema is the contract: the backend owns it, the app and the console generate their own types, no code crosses a repo, and migrations are additive only.
Ask Bunny needs a signed-in person; the model words a reply the server validates, and a spend breaker stops it.

flows.title: A client action
steps: The Flutter app (supabase-dart) and the console browser (`src/integrations/supabase/`) both call Supabase REST/Auth directly for reads and simple per-user writes, enforced by row-level security — no server sits in between for these (app CLAUDE.md "Stack", console CLAUDE.md "Stack").

A privileged verb — hosting ops, moderation, payments, check-in — goes through a named Edge Function running as `service_role` instead: `manager-actions` for host writes, `admin-actions` for every one of the console's 11 admin verbs via `src/lib/admin-ctx.tsx`'s `act()` (console CLAUDE.md "/admin — real identity"), `sign-week-pass`/`door-sync` for check-in.
Functions start CLOSED — a migration adding one must explicitly `grant execute` to its real caller; the backstop is `tools/check-fn-grants.sh`, run after every `db reset` (backend CLAUDE.md "Stack").

flows.title: External event data
steps: `tools/ingest.py`, the Luma puller (`tools/pull_luma_nyc.py`), the Ticketmaster Discovery API puller, and any approved `bunny-connectors` integration all push through the one door: the `ingest-events` edge function, service-role, provenance mandatory on every row.

A brand-new connector's first contact lands STAGED (invisible to users) until approved once in the admin panel; a re-push of the same `source_uid` upserts, and an update to a claimed (host-edited) event files an `event_feed_proposals` row instead of overwriting it (connectors CLAUDE.md).

flows.title: A ticket purchase (TEST mode)
steps: App or console calls `create-checkout-session` / `create-ticket-checkout`, which talks to Stripe in TEST mode (`livemode:false`).

Stripe calls back `payments-webhook`, which writes `orders`/`order_items`/`tickets` — money in this build is simulated by design, Stripe-shaped SQL (`seam_registry`/`seam_ledger` audit the autopass trail per platform-architecture research).

flows.title: Push and auth email
steps: `send-push` / `notify-worker` deliver push through APNs to the app.
Supabase Auth's own SMTP config (Google Workspace relay) sends magic-link, invite and recovery email directly — this path does not go through an edge function.

flows.title: Door check-in
steps: `sign-week-pass` mints/verifies the rotating pass proof; `door-sync` handles idempotent bulk check-in sync for the app's door mode and the console's `/manage` door screens.

flows.title: Cross-repo release (backend-first)
steps: A schema or contract change always lands in `bunny-backend` first: an additive migration under `supabase/migrations/` (never edit an applied one), then `supabase db push` to the one hosted project.

`bunny-app` (Dart) and `bunny-console` (`types.ts`) each regenerate their own types from the new schema — no code crosses the repo boundary, only the schema contract (root CLAUDE.md "Dependency direction").

The app ships via TestFlight (`bunny-backend/tools/testflight-release.sh`, the App Store Connect credentials live only in that repo) — always kicked off from `bunny-backend`, never from `bunny-app` (app CLAUDE.md "Ship"). The console's production deploy is a manual ritual from `console/`; git pushes build branch PREVIEWS only (anon key only, service-role key removed from Preview), never production (QF08D993C).

`bunny-connectors` never touches schema/UI/secrets directly — it only ever speaks the frozen `ingest-events` contract, so it needs no coordinated release with the other three repos (connectors CLAUDE.md).

flows.title: Errors and product analytics
steps: The app reports errors to Sentry project "bunny-app"; the console reports to the separate Sentry project "bunny-console" — same org, different projects, deliberately not shared.
Product analytics goes to the single PostHog project "bunny-beta".
